# Pattern selection

Select by information need, not visual shape. Check profile compatibility before adapting an example.

| Pattern             | Purpose                                                                                        | Information needs                                                                              | Profiles                                        | Variants                                      | Avoid this misuse                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action-cluster`    | Group a small number of high-value actions in clear priority order.                            | offer primary and secondary actions, group document actions                                    | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | primary-secondary, compact                    | Do not turn ordinary navigation or a toolbar with many controls into an action cluster.             |
| `closing-field`     | End a document with a memorable synthesis or focused call to action.                           | close with a synthesis, end with a call to action, state the final takeaway                    | rail-document, review-packet                    | synthesis, call-to-action                     | Do not use a closing field to introduce new evidence or several competing next steps.               |
| `comparison-bridge` | Contrast two states or explain a deliberate before-to-after transition.                        | compare before and after, contrast two states, explain a transition                            | rail-document, review-packet                    | bridge, before-after                          | Do not use a comparison bridge for more than two states or for a multi-step process.                |
| `content-card`      | Present one bounded idea with optional category, state, or supporting detail.                  | present a bounded idea, group peer findings, show a compact concept                            | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | standard, compact, finding                    | Do not default to a grid of cards when sequence, hierarchy, or comparison is the real relationship. |
| `decision-ledger`   | Record numbered questions, decisions, or commitments with durable rationale.                   | record decisions and rationale, list numbered commitments, track resolved questions            | rail-document, review-packet                    | numbered, commitments                         | Do not use a decision ledger as a task list or chronological process.                               |
| `diagram-frame`     | Present, caption, scroll, and optionally focus a technical diagram.                            | frame a technical diagram, present a wide relationship view, caption an svg diagram            | rail-document, review-packet                    | plain, grid, focusable                        | Do not use a diagram frame around decorative art or a simple fact that prose explains better.       |
| `disclosure-group`  | Keep secondary evidence available without interrupting the main reading or task path.          | hide secondary evidence until requested, provide optional detail, group supplementary evidence | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | standard                                      | Do not hide required decisions, errors, or primary task controls in a disclosure.                   |
| `empty-state`       | Explain why a bounded application region has no items and offer one useful recovery action.    | explain no search results, show an empty data region                                           | application-shell                               | no-data, no-results                           | Do not use an empty state while data is loading or when an error prevented retrieval.               |
| `evidence-matrix`   | Compare structured evidence or attributes across shared categories.                            | compare structured evidence, show attributes across categories, present tabular evidence       | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | table, evidence                               | Do not force prose, process steps, or a two-state rhetorical contrast into a matrix.                |
| `flow-row`          | Show a short ordered transformation across peer steps.                                         | show a short transformation, explain a linear pipeline, connect peer steps                     | rail-document, review-packet                    | sequence, pipeline, build-line                | Do not squeeze a long process, branches, or exception paths into a flow row.                        |
| `form-field`        | Collect one labelled value with help, validation, and error feedback.                          | collect a labelled value, show field validation                                                | application-shell                               | text, select, validation                      | Do not use placeholder text as the only label or validate before the user can act.                  |
| `layer-stack`       | Explain ordered conceptual or technical layers and their responsibilities.                     | explain ordered layers, show responsibility by layer                                           | rail-document, review-packet                    | standard, storage                             | Do not use a layer stack for chronological steps or peers with no dependency order.                 |
| `phase-timeline`    | Explain staged delivery or sequential work packages.                                           | show a staged delivery sequence, explain release phases, present sequential work packages      | rail-document, review-packet                    | timeline, slices                              | Do not use a phase timeline for runtime behavior or unordered priorities.                           |
| `process-spine`     | Show a longer ordered process with detail or status at each step.                              | explain a detailed process, show ordered work with status                                      | rail-document, review-packet                    | steps, ladder                                 | Do not use the process spine for release phases or an unordered checklist.                          |
| `section-lead`      | Establish a section title, context, and concise reading cue.                                   | introduce a document section, orient a numbered section                                        | rail-document, review-packet                    | plain, numbered                               | Do not use a section lead as a decorative wrapper around every small card.                          |
| `signal-strip`      | Summarize several compact facts, metrics, or concepts for quick scanning.                      | summarize compact facts, show a small metric set, surface quick signals                        | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | chips, metrics, quick-calls                   | Do not use a signal strip for facts that need explanation or comparison across many columns.        |
| `statement-hero`    | Introduce the artifact identity and central argument at statement scale.                       | introduce a central argument, establish artifact identity                                      | rail-document, review-packet                    | statement, masthead                           | Do not repeat a statement hero at ordinary section boundaries.                                      |
| `status-banner`     | Report task feedback, warnings, recoverable errors, or loading state near the affected region. | report application status, show a recoverable error, indicate loading                          | application-shell                               | information, success, warning, error, loading | Do not use a status banner for field-specific validation or permanent explanatory prose.            |
| `terminal-panel`    | Present commands, output, formulas, or exact textual artifacts.                                | show an exact command, present terminal output, display exact technical text                   | rail-document, review-packet, application-shell | command, output, formula                      | Do not put ordinary prose in a terminal panel to make it appear technical.                          |
| `triage-columns`    | Sort decisions into keep, remove, and defer categories.                                        | triage decisions, sort keep cut and defer, group disposition choices                           | rail-document, review-packet                    | keep-cut-defer, two-way                       | Do not use triage columns for neutral categories or evidence without a disposition.                 |
| `verdict-callout`   | Give a conclusion, correction, or governing rule more weight than body prose.                  | emphasize a conclusion, state a governing rule, call out a correction                          | rail-document, review-packet                    | verdict, rule, thesis, warning                | Do not place routine notes in a verdict callout or stack several without analysis between them.     |

Application-only patterns are experimental. Keep their status visible in the artifact.
